analysis.title: GOAL: Global Opportunity Asset Locator. Outlook for 2027: Finding Balance Around Peak Growth
key_insights: GS stays modestly pro-risk for 2027 but wants more balance across and within assets. Nominal and earnings growth are expected to peak after the 2026 AI capex boom and the energy-driven inflation boost.

Allocation (12-month): overweight equities and 10y government bonds, underweight credit, neutral cash and commodities. Within equities: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex-Japan and EM, underweight Europe.

Global real GDP growth for 2027 is forecast at 2.8%, 0.1pp above consensus. Global headline inflation is forecast to fall from 3.7% to 2.6% (core 2.9% to 2.4%). GS is above consensus on US growth (2.5% vs 2.3%) and below on Europe (0.9% vs 1.3%).

Earnings growth is expected to peak and slow materially as the AI capex impulse plateaus. GS still forecasts about 17% earnings growth for MSCI AC World, above trend, which is consistent with slower but positive equity returns versus bonds.

Historically equities consolidate around nominal growth peaks but keep rising afterward, especially when falling inflation drives the peak and real growth holds. Drawdowns were larger when growth slowed sharply, for example in a US recession.

Equity valuations have already de-rated in 2026, particularly semiconductors and the wider Tech sector, on concerns about AI-related cash flow and profits. S&P 500 earnings are 60% above their 10-year average and ROE is at a record, so markets are already discounting some decline in profitability.

Consensus expects ROE to fall for every mega-cap Tech stock from 2027, by an average of 7pp, as AI capex makes business models more asset-heavy. GS expects opportunity to shift from building AI to using AI, with applications, adopters and productivity beneficiaries broadening beyond capex names.

Dispersion within equities may be near a peak, which could mark a trough in equity volatility. Average S&P 500 pairwise correlations are near 60-year lows, which has anchored index volatility. Broader correlations or a sharper growth slowdown could lift volatility.

GS favours balancing Tech-heavy benchmarks with quality, defensive and high dividend/buyback stocks, plus selective growth exposure such as US hyperscalers. Low-volatility and high-yield styles have become uncorrelated with the market for the first time on record.

Bonds are expected to be a better equity buffer as nominal growth peaks. Higher starting yields, US longer-dated real yields near 3% and easing inflation should make equity/bond correlations more negative. Hourly S&P 500 vs 10y correlation has been clearly negative since October.

Rates forecasts: 10y UST 4.6% and Gilts 4.8% by end-2027, Bunds 3.1%, JGBs 2.75%. GS expects greater curve flattening if policy rate upside risks materialise. The OAT-Bund spread is forecast at 130bps by mid-27 and 100bps by end-27, with French political risk higher.

GS economists expect only two further Fed hikes, and markets are seen as close to pricing peak hawkishness. Historically 60/40 portfolios were range-bound until the US 2-year yield peaked and then performed better. Near-term rate shock risk remains, so bond allocation hedges into year-end are suggested.

Credit is underweight: modest spread widening is expected (gradual in USD, front-loaded in 1H27 in EUR), plus rising supply (US IG and HY issuance $2.8tn in 2027 vs $2.6tn in 2026) and releveraging. AI-related issuers face episodic widening. Prefer USD over EUR and IG over HY in USD. Equities are preferred over credit, as in the late 1990s.

Commodities are neutral: near-zero BCOM total return is expected in 2027 after a 24% YTD gain, on energy normalisation. 2027 average Brent is forecast at $88/bbl and TTF at €45/MWh. Shipping attacks and infrastructure damage are near-term upside price risks. The end-2027 gold forecast was cut to $4,650/toz after hawkish Fed headwinds.

FX: the dollar is expected to weaken in 2027 as its 2026 supports (sticky inflation, resilience to energy prices, AI investment expectations) turn into headwinds. GS expects a reversal in commodity-sensitive currencies, a more durable policy support for the yen, and 12m targets of EUR/USD 1.15 and USD/JPY 150.

Overlay ideas: VIX calls are the best hedge against a rate shock, followed by equity puts on rate-sensitive indices (Russell, STOXX 600). Long-dated call replacements are preferred for equity right-tail exposure. In a growth scare with a central bank cushion, bond calls, rate receivers, USD/JPY puts and unhedged JGBs screen well.

Front-end receiver swaptions are called a very convex 1-year recession hedge, with a payoff in past recessions larger than an OTM S&P 500 put. Selling 1m receivers on 10y rates gives an almost 3pp annualised yield pickup. TIPS look attractive with elevated real yields and little breakeven repricing.

Positioning has reset in Q4 2026. The Risk Appetite Indicator has been negative since October, hedge funds de-grossed, retail leverage peaked, and the aggregate positioning and sentiment indicator sits at the 38th percentile. Margin debt is about $1.5tn, around 2% of US market cap, and US household equity allocation is very high.

2026 review: energy commodities led, equities were strong in 1H on AI earnings and weaker in 2H on higher rates and AI concerns. Value and defensives outperformed in 2H. Precious metals and bitcoin were the worst performers as central banks turned hawkish.

Key risks: a larger AI capex slowdown, earlier AI labour-market disruption, renewed Middle East energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and persistent fiscal concerns. The 2027 calendar includes the French presidential election (April/May), FOMC meetings, a likely US debt limit in Q1 and the ECB presidency transition in October.

sector_views.rationale: Selective growth exposure. Long-duration growth companies gain value as growth slows, and hyperscalers have strong albeit slower earnings growth and strong balance sheets.
Cyclical earnings tied to AI capex have de-rated and index concentration keeps volatility elevated. Growth in earnings tailwinds is weakening.
Low-volatility sectors outperformed and re-rated versus Tech since summer. GS favours quality, defensive and high dividend/buyback stocks to balance Tech-heavy benchmarks.
Listed as credit key ideas within the underweight credit stance.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts roughly 17% earnings growth for MSCI AC World in 2027, above trend across regions, excluding mega-cap tech other income from private investment stakes. This is a GS forecast, not a reported figure.
Earnings growth is expected to peak and decline from elevated 2026 levels, driven by the AI capex boom plateauing alongside nominal GDP growth.
S&P 500 earnings are 60% above their 10-year rolling average and operating ROE has risen by more than 400bps in 2026 to a record. Current ROE is about 21%.
Consensus expects ROE to decline for every mega-cap Tech stock from next year, by an average of 7pp, as capex raises depreciation and asset intensity.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS economists are 0.1pp above consensus and potential. Sturdy growth with relatively stable labour markets supports the constructive nominal growth peak scenario.
GS is above consensus on resilient investment.
GS is below consensus on tighter financial conditions and higher energy prices biting this winter, which supports the Europe underweight.
Easing energy prices and fading base effects lower inflation, limiting further central bank tightening.
Supports less hawkish policy than market pricing in most regions except Japan.
GS economists see limited US recession risk and markets close to pricing peak hawkishness, supporting a gradual decline in US 2-year yields.
Largest forecast bond rally among major markets, from a current 5.11%.
Moderating energy prices drive near-zero BCOM total return. Intensifying shipping attacks and infrastructure damage are upside risks.
Persian Gulf LNG exports have rebounded to more than 60% of pre-war levels so far in November.
Forecast cut on hawkish Fed headwinds, while GS stays constructive long term on central bank demand.

macro_indicators.indicator: US IG and HY bond issuance
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from $2.6 trillion in 2026, adding supply pressure to credit.

crypto_views: Bitcoin was among the worst-performing assets in 2026 as central banks turned more hawkish, alongside precious metals.

risk_factors: AI capex slows more sharply than expected, or AI monetisation disappoints against cash flow commitments and rising depreciation.
AI-related labour market disruption arrives earlier than expected, deepening growth concerns later in 2027.
Renewed energy shocks from Middle East tensions, including shipping attacks and infrastructure damage.
More aggressive Fed tightening or renewed fiscal concerns push bond yields higher.
Persistent fiscal concerns and higher government debt, with French OAT spreads as the relative pricing channel.
Rising leverage and heavy debt-funded issuance across the AI ecosystem pressures credit and equity valuations.
Concentration of semiconductors in Asia and EM indices keeps index-level volatility elevated.
Tech dominance: TMT is almost 40% of global equity market cap, and 40-50% of private market value is linked to Tech.
The DAA model excludes AI-related earnings swings and may understate both upside and downside risks.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 lists GS asset allocation: equities OW (S&P 500 and TOPIX up arrows, MSCI Asia Pac ex Japan neutral, STOXX Europe 600 down), 10y government bonds OW, cash N, commodities N, credit UW.
Exhibit 35 states the aggregate positioning and sentiment indicator is at the 38th percentile.
Exhibit 43 states margin debt grew to c.$1.5tn, around 2% of US market cap.
Exhibit 12 states US earnings are well above trend and return on equity is near all-time highs.
Exhibit 16 states unusually low correlations across stocks have anchored equity volatility.
vol_and_positioning: VIX calls are the best hedge against a rate shock. VIX sensitivity to growth pricing relative to implied vol remains high by historical standards despite the recent rise in vol of vol.
Equity puts rank second as rate-shock hedges, particularly on rate-sensitive indices such as the Russell or the STOXX 600.

Replacing equities with long-dated call options is preferred for hedging the right tail in a spot-up/vol-up backdrop. Calendar collars, put spreads and long-dated call replacements worked best in 2026 while most short-dated put overlays were too costly versus realised volatility.

S&P 500 equal-weight calls are cheap versus S&P 500 calls, making switches attractive. China large-cap volatility is very low versus Taiwan's, so selling Taiwan calls to buy China H calls balances AI exposure.

Selling 1m receiver swaptions on 10-year rates offers an almost 3pp annualised yield pickup. Front-end receiver swaptions are a convex 1-year recession hedge. Energy-exposed asset vols are low versus Brent implied vol, with EUR/NOK upside highlighted as an energy-relief hedge.

Positioning: Risk Appetite Indicator negative since October, hedge funds de-grossed, retail leverage peaked, aggregate positioning and sentiment at the 38th percentile. Margin debt is about $1.5tn, around 2% of US market cap.

S&P 500 average pairwise correlations are near 60-year lows and the share of stocks with negative betas rose above Tech Bubble levels. Dispersion may be near a peak, which could mark a trough in equity volatility.
Equity put-selling may become a more attractive source of carry than credit if volatility is higher.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions could renew energy price pressure. Intensifying shipping attacks and infrastructure damage are near-term upside risks to oil and gas prices.

Persian Gulf LNG exports averaged 33% of pre-war levels in October and more than 60% so far in November. GS base case sees Mideast oil supply above its 2025 average via ship-to-ship transfers and new pipelines.
French presidential election (first round 18 April, second round 2 May) is a key European political risk, with OAT spreads the main fiscal-risk expression.
Democratic sweep at the US midterm elections is cited as a source of more regulation that could slow AI capex.
China remains a drag on global growth through weak domestic demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have de-rated over three years on capex concerns, but stronger cloud revenues and lower AI capex could support them. Opportunities broaden to AI applications, adopters and productivity gains.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex nears a peak, monetisation lags cash flow commitments and rising depreciation, and consensus expects ROE to fall by an average of 7pp across mega-cap Tech. Debt-funded AI buildout adds credit and valuation risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A larger-than-expected AI capex slowdown or earlier-than-expected AI-related labour market disruption would deepen the growth concerns later in 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Easing energy prices and normalising inflation limit further tightening, with only two more Fed hikes expected. A US 2-year yield peak has historically brought relief to equities and 60/40 portfolios.
tension_points.bear_case: More aggressive Fed tightening or renewed fiscal concerns could push yields higher and weigh on balanced portfolios near term. Market pricing is more hawkish than the GS baseline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A clear peak in US 2-year yields would end the range-bound 60/40 pattern. Failure to peak, with higher rates from Fed tightening or fiscal concerns, would invalidate the rates relief call.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities have de-rated this year and offer greater upside convexity in favourable AI scenarios. In the late 1990s equities kept rising while credit lagged.
tension_points.bear_case: Equity volatility is likely to rise as earnings growth slows, lowering risk-adjusted returns. A sharp growth slowdown or US recession would produce larger equity drawdowns.

theme_stances.key_argument: Nominal and earnings growth peak after the AI capex boom, but peaking need not end the bull market, so GS stays modestly pro-risk with more diversification.
theme_stances.evidence: We remain modestly pro-risk but favour more balance across and within assets

theme_stances.key_argument: Tight spreads, releveraging and rising issuance limit credit returns while equities offer more upside in favourable AI scenarios.
theme_stances.evidence: We still prefer equities to credit

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher starting yields and easing inflation improve bonds' return prospects and make equity/bond correlations more negative.
theme_stances.evidence: Bonds should offer a better buffer against equity weakness as nominal growth
